header.running_head: The Fear that the Khulafaa had for Allaah

blocks.text: and made sustenance widespread.' Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, 'Are you praising me for my leadership, O son of Abbaas?' 'For other reasons as well,' I replied. He then said, 'I swear by the Being Who controls my life that I wish to emerge from it just as I had entered into it without any rewards and without any sin." [^1]

Another narration states that Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) said to Hadhrat Umar (RA), "Accept the glad tidings of Jannah for you have been in the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ for a very long time. Thereafter, when you became the Ameer of the Mu'mineen, you lent tremendous strength to them and fulfilled the trust placed on your shoulders." Hadhrat Umar (RA) responded by saying, "As for the glad tidings of Jannah that you have given me, I swear by the Being besides Whom there is none worthy of worship that if I owned the world and all its contents, I would have offered it as ransom to be saved from the frightening scene that lies ahead of me. As for what you have said about my leadership over the Mu'mineen, I swear by Allaah that I wish it were a clean sheet without any rewards in my favour nor any punishment. As for what you have mentioned about my companionship with Rasulullaah ﷺ, this is something (precious, for which I can expect great rewards)." [^2]

blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr
blocks.text: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Ubayd bin Umayr narrates that a lengthy narration in which he states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked those around him to help him sit up. When they did this, he asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) to repeat what he had said. When Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) repeated his words, Hadhrat Umar (RA) asked, "Will you testify to this before Allaah on the day you meet Him?" "Certainly," replied Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA). Hadhrat Umar (RA) then became very happy and was pleased. [^3]
The Narration of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Miswar Concerning the Fear Hadhrat Umar (RA) had for Allaah

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "Umar (RA)'s head was on my lap when he was suffering the illness that eventually claimed his life. 'Put my head on the ground,' he said to me. I said, 'What difference would it make if it is on my lap or on the ground?' However, he again ordered me to place it on the ground and I complied. He then said, 'My mother and I are destroyed if my Rabb does not have mercy on me!'"

Hadhrat Miswar reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was stabbed, he said, "If I possessed enough gold to fill the earth, I would have given it to ransom myself from the punishment of Allaah before I can even see it." [^4]

Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.52). Tabraani has also reported the narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) in great detail, as has Abu Ya'la reported it from Abu Raafi, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.9 Pg.76). Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.254) has also reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA).
